answer: One workable design: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because garden only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. In practice shale is enforced by the ledger itself: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
